about.text: A soft cottage-type cheese from the Ethiopian highlands. Fermented whole milk (ergo) is churned for butter, and the leftover buttermilk is heated until curd and whey separate. The curd is then drained through cloth. About six litres of buttermilk make one kilogram of ayib.

sources.text: The photograph, its author and its licence, from its page.

facts.v: E. coli O157:H7 survives in ayib; heating the buttermilk to 70 °C stopped it
Eaten beside spicy dishes such as kitfo and kocho, to soften their heat
A staple across ethnic groups, cheap and affordable
